role: Six individual source/caller applicability proposals; mandatory canonical integration remains pending

upstream_originals.scope: Shared immutable upstream commit/blob/complete-patch identity only; not another line's consumer or peer qualification.

reviews.decision: Do not add the experimental type/color inspection APIs or versioned M3 palette internals to the owned Material16 facade. Its original M2 constructors and palette helpers remain independently owned; the current public Material namespace retains its own newer API.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Adds primary/secondary/tertiary/neutral/error palettes to the experimental versioned M3 internals. The owned Material16 model uses its original primary/accent/warn configs; no owned constructor or bridge produces or consumes this new internals object.

Exposes get-theme-type and get-theme-color only through private-prefixed experimental exports. They are outside the authentic 25-function Material16 facade; the compiler confirms the current peer exports them in its separate namespace without adding them to the facade.

Adds type, role-color and palette-color inspection with M3 validation, arity checks and unsupported-role/palette/hue diagnostics. These new getters initially reject legacy theme maps; transplanting them would add a modern API mirror rather than repair an original palette helper.

Corrects spelling and formatting in the new token-system validation error. This module is peer-owned and absent from the owned Sass sources; existing historical helper diagnostics and immutable expected CSS are not changed.

Reformats the M2 version test and changes its equivalent expected content assertion to a regular expression. This is an upstream inspection test, not evidence that the original or candidate Sass suites executed.

Adds M3 type, role/palette color, invalid key/hue and argument-count tests. Those tests explain the new inspection contract; they do not authorize new legacy exports or replacement of historical palette/theme calls.

reviews.decision: Do not add the new M3 typography inspection getter or typescale contract to the finite historical facade. Existing historical typography helpers remain exported under their original names; current peer typography inspection stays in the peer namespace.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Adds a private-prefixed typography inspection export to the developing API. The historical facade retains the original typography functions and does not mirror this newer getter into its public or historical private namespace.

Defines the M3 display/headline/title/label/body typescale names and allowed font properties. These constants belong to the new inspection module; the owned typography model continues using the independently owned historical configuration levels.

Adds get-theme-typography with M3 validation, typescale/property checks and token-name lookup. It explicitly rejects legacy maps at this stage; the original font-family/font-size/font-weight/line-height/letter-spacing helpers remain the owned contract.

Changes the M2 version fixture from content to an interpolated custom property while keeping version zero. This test-output rewrite is not copied into an immutable historical golden or counted as an executed product assertion.
Changes the M3 version fixture to an interpolated custom property while retaining version one. It documents the experimental module and does not change the legacy facade's theme representation.
Changes the M3 type fixture to a custom property with the same light result. This affects only the upstream inspection fixture; no owned selector, theme-map key or consumer namespace is renamed.

Uses a real color declaration rather than content for the role-color success fixture. The new API remains outside the owned legacy function set, while current Material keeps its own public implementation.
Changes the invalid-role fixture's CSS property while preserving its expected rejection. This is reviewed upstream intent, not a substitute for original legacy palette argument or error tests.
Uses a color declaration and exact string expectation for the tertiary palette success case. Its M3 hue semantics are not imposed on the historical numeric/A-hue palette helpers.
Changes only the CSS property in the invalid-palette fixture. Historical palette-name and value behavior remains covered by its separate original contracts, not this new inspection API test.
Changes only the CSS property in the invalid-hue fixture. The legacy facade continues accepting its original palette hue conventions without adding the M3 inspection getter.

Changes the arity fixture's property and adds typography value plus invalid typescale/property tests. The added Google Sans/M3 expectations are scoped to the new getter and never replace original typography or CSS goldens.

reviews.decision: Do not add the new density inspection getter to the Material16 facade. Its original get-density-config API and owned component/bridge clamping remain separate from versioned-theme inspection; no consumer call or theme map changes are required.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Adds the private-prefixed density inspection export. The authentic Material16 facade exposes get-density-config instead; adding this newer getter would expand the finite legacy API rather than preserve it.

Adds a versioned-theme density-scale lookup that explicitly rejects legacy theme objects. Owned density config retrieval and component-specific clamping continue using their historical helpers and independently owned bridge code.

Corrects the unsupported typography-property fixture and adds an M3 density-scale-zero assertion. These upstream test changes are read for intent; no claim is made that their original test runner or full Sass gate executed.

reviews.decision: Do not transplant the new theme-has predicate and inspection diagnostics into the legacy facade. The owned historical API does not expose or directly call the inspection family, and direct current-peer calls remain public override mixins.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Adds private-theme-has to the developing inspection export list. The legacy facade does not acquire this newer theme-system predicate; current peer consumers retain it through the separate public Material namespace.

Adds a color-information presence check before reading a versioned theme type. This changes the new inspection API's diagnostics and does not repair or replace the owned Material16 light/dark theme constructors.
Adds a color-information check before role lookup. Owned palette helpers use original M2 palette/config inputs; the compiler and source census show no direct owned call to this inspection function.
Adds a color-information check before palette inspection. The historical facade's get-color-from-palette behavior remains separate and is not redirected to this versioned-theme getter.
Adds a typography-information check before typescale lookup. This concerns the new M3 inspection function, while the original 25-function owned namespace and its typography helpers remain intact.

Adds density-information checking and the base/color/typography/density presence predicate. Its versioned internals and initially legacy-rejecting semantics are outside the finite historical model, so this implementation is not transplanted.

Removes local M2/M3 fixture-construction interfaces and helper functions. Their replacement with explicit/default theme construction is a test refactor, not a change to the add-on's public constructors or consumer theme maps.

Replaces the M2 version fixture helper with explicit palette, typography and density settings. This fixes the upstream fixture setup without changing owned defaults or deriving a new historical expected value from the candidate.
Uses the experimental default M3 theme in the version fixture. Its version-one expectation belongs to the upstream module; no source or runtime floor is inferred from that test alone.
Uses the default M3 theme for type inspection. The owned facade still exports only historical helper functions, with separate peer namespace visibility measured on each maintained line.
Replaces custom M3 colors with default colors and updates the two color expectations accordingly. These fixture-dependent values do not justify changing any original palette or CSS golden.

Replaces the custom M3 palette fixture with default palette data and its corresponding expected color. Invalid-palette rejection remains an upstream new-API assertion and is not a legacy palette behavior change.

Replaces the custom theme in the invalid-hue fixture with the default M3 theme. The expected invalid-hue error remains scoped to the modern inspection API, without changing owned historical hue interpretation.
Replaces the custom theme in the wrong-argument-count fixture. The new API's arity check is reviewed as intent; it creates no new required legacy function or consumer call rewrite.
Uses the experimental default theme for typography inspection. The owned typography configuration model and original function names remain the source of legacy values.

Updates font expectations from the removed Google Sans fixture to the default Roboto stack. This is an upstream test-oracle adjustment caused by changed fixture input, not authority to update retained historical typography goldens.
Uses the default M3 theme for invalid typescale validation. This new getter's supported M3 scale list does not replace the historical typography level names or mixin arguments.
Uses the default M3 theme for invalid typography-property validation. The resulting expected error remains an upstream inspection API contract and is not reported as executed legacy behavior.

Uses the default density fixture and adds theme-system presence plus missing-color/typography/density errors. These tests define the new versioned-theme API; the add-on keeps its historical config helpers and public peer override boundary.

reviews.decision: Do not transplant the formatting and semicolon fixes for the peer-owned inspection module into owned legacy Sass. The module is loaded through current public Material imports but has no owned inspection implementation or direct owned inspection call to repair.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Moves @else onto its own line after the same closing brace. Role/palette dispatch conditions and calls remain unchanged in the peer-owned inspection module; no equivalent code exists in the owned historical API to patch.

Adds the missing semicolon to the density-presence return expression. This is a syntax correction in the newer inspection implementation and does not alter a historical helper, consumer theme map or legacy CSS output.

reviews.decision: Do not copy or call through the new M2 inspection adapter. Its support for historical-shaped maps adds modern getter contracts rather than repairing original helper names; the facade keeps the independently owned Material16 model and public override bridge boundary.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: Imports a new M2 inspection module and removes the introductory comment. The owned Sass facade does not import this peer-private module or forward its newer API; its M2 model remains independently owned.

Dispatches theme-type inspection by version, adding M2 delegation and retaining M3 color checks with unknown-version rejection. This extends the new getter's accepted inputs rather than changing the original light/dark constructors.

Adds argument validation and version dispatch to color inspection. Although the new API now accepts M2 maps, its extra public contract is still absent from the Material16 inventory; historical palette helper names and arguments are preserved.

Adds M2 delegation for typography and density, keeps the M3 checks/token lookups, and rejects unknown versions. The original get-typography-config/get-density-config and font helpers are not redirected to the current compatibility implementation.

Adds version dispatch for theme-has while retaining the M3 system-key checks. The owned legacy model does not gain this modern predicate or start interpreting its maps through peer inspection internals.

Adds the complete M2 adapter: theme type, palette access, typography properties, density clamping and system presence. It calls old helpers but exposes new APIs; copying or calling through it would violate the finite independent historical facade requirement.

Adds M2 inspection success and presence fixtures using original palettes, font levels and density. These confirm the new adapter's intended reach without making it part of the older facade or replacing independent historical function-value/CSS tests.

limitations: No full function-value/signature/CSS/Sass/native/browser/SSR/compiler/runtime or peer-floor gate is claimed.
Main is measured against installed22.1.7; advertised22.1.6 qualification remains required.
Current peer modules may use their own inspection internals; no owned private import or copied modern API is authorized.
The canonical ledger still requires explicit typed per-SHA admission; these reports alone do not clear it.
